name: Foundational Spanish
credits: Hand-curated against DELE A1 specifications + Davies' top-2000 frequency dictionary. Sequenced for first-150-minute pedagogical depth.

levels.name: First Contact
levels.can_do: Greet someone, introduce myself, ask and answer basic personal questions. Understand slow, clear speech on immediate topics.

units.title: Greetings & farewells
units.goal: Greet at different times of day, say goodbye, ask how someone is.

phrases.en: Hi, how are you?
Very well, thanks. And you?
Good morning, ma'am.
Goodbye, see you tomorrow.
Sorry, I don't understand.

units.grammar_note: Spanish has informal (tú) and formal (usted) address. Use tú with peers; usted with strangers and elders.

units.title: Introducing yourself
units.goal: Say your name, ask someone else's name, give your nationality.

phrases.en: What's your name? My name is Ana.
Pleased to meet you. Likewise (m.).
I'm American. And you?

phrases.target: Él es mi amigo, se llama Luis.
phrases.en: He's my friend, his name is Luis.

units.grammar_note: Spanish adjectives agree with the speaker's gender: encantado (m.) / encantada (f.).

units.title: Numbers 0-20 & age
units.goal: Count 0-20, ask and say someone's age.

phrases.en: I'm twenty years old.
How old are you? — I'm eighteen.
My friend is fifteen.

units.grammar_note: Spanish uses tener (to have) for age — literally 'I have 20 years', not 'I am 20'.

units.title: Family
units.goal: Name immediate family, describe basic relationships.

phrases.target: Tengo dos hermanos y una hermana.
phrases.en: I have two brothers and one sister.
My mother's name is Carmen.
My grandparents live in Mexico.

units.grammar_note: Plural family terms default to masculine: hermanos = brothers OR mixed siblings.

units.title: Days, time, today
units.goal: Say the day, time of day, ask what time it is.

phrases.en: Today is Monday.

phrases.target: ¿Qué hora es? — Son las tres y media.
phrases.en: What time is it? — It's three thirty.
Tomorrow is Saturday.

units.grammar_note: Days are masculine; lowercase in Spanish (unlike English). 'es la una' (singular) for 1:00, 'son las…' for all other hours.

units.title: Food & ordering
units.goal: Name common foods/drinks, order at a café, say what you like.

phrases.target: Quiero un café con leche, por favor.
phrases.en: I'd like a coffee with milk, please.
I like fruit.
Do you have still water? — Yes, of course.
The bill, please.

units.grammar_note: 'Me gusta' literally is 'it pleases me' — agrees with the *thing*, not the speaker. Me gusta**n** las frutas (plural).

units.title: Colors & describing things
units.goal: Describe objects and people with basic adjectives.

phrases.target: La casa es grande y blanca.
phrases.en: The house is big and white.
My sister is very tall.
The coffee is good today.

units.grammar_note: Most adjectives change ending: rojo (m.) / roja (f.) / rojos (m. pl.) / rojas (f. pl.). 'azul' / 'verde' / 'grande' don't change for gender, only number.

units.title: Body & feeling unwell
units.goal: Name body parts, describe how you feel, say what hurts.

phrases.en: I have a headache.
I'm tired today.
My sister is sick.

units.grammar_note: Spanish has two verbs for 'to be': ser (permanent) and estar (state/location). Use estar for moods, locations, and temporary states.

units.title: Daily routine verbs
units.goal: Describe a daily routine using simple present-tense verbs.

phrases.en: I get up at seven.

phrases.target: Trabajo y estudio todos los días.
phrases.en: I work and study every day.
I speak a little Spanish.

units.grammar_note: Spanish regular -ar verbs in 'I' form: hablar → hablo, trabajar → trabajo, estudiar → estudio. The pattern is consistent.

units.title: Home & rooms
units.goal: Name parts of a house, say where you live, describe your home.

phrases.en: I live in a small apartment.
My house has three bedrooms.
I live with my family.

units.grammar_note: Spanish verbs ending in -ir (vivir, escribir): yo vivo, tú vives, él/ella vive — same pattern as -er verbs in singular.

units.title: City & directions
units.goal: Name common places in a city, ask and give simple directions.

phrases.target: ¿Dónde está el banco? — A la derecha.
phrases.en: Where's the bank? — On the right.

phrases.target: El hotel está cerca de aquí.
phrases.en: The hotel is near here.
How do I get to the museum? — Straight ahead.

units.grammar_note: Spanish prepositional contractions: a + el → al, de + el → del. 'al museo' (to the museum), 'del banco' (of the bank).

units.title: Weather & seasons
units.goal: Describe the weather, name the seasons, talk about climate.

phrases.en: Today is very hot.

phrases.target: En invierno nieva en las montañas.
phrases.en: In winter it snows in the mountains.

phrases.target: Me gusta la primavera porque hace buen tiempo.
phrases.en: I like spring because the weather is nice.

units.grammar_note: Spanish weather uses 'hacer' (to do/make): hace sol, hace calor. Some use the verb directly: llueve (it rains), nieva (it snows).

levels.name: Waystage
levels.can_do: Communicate in simple routine tasks. Describe in simple terms my background and immediate environment. Discuss past events and future plans.

units.title: Talking about yesterday (preterite)
units.goal: Narrate completed events in the recent past using regular preterite and a few high-frequency irregulars.

vocab.gloss: I went / I was (preterite of ir/ser)

phrases.en: Yesterday I spoke with my mother.
Last night I ate at a restaurant.

phrases.target: La semana pasada fui a la ciudad.
phrases.en: Last week I went to the city.
What did you do yesterday? — I saw a movie.
I had a very long day.

units.grammar_note: Regular preterite endings: -ar verbs take -é/-aste/-ó; -er and -ir share -í/-iste/-ió. The yo and él forms always carry written accents.

units.title: How things used to be (imperfect)
units.goal: Describe past habits, repeated actions, and background using the imperfect tense.

phrases.target: Cuando era niño, vivía en México.
phrases.en: When I was a child, I lived in Mexico.
I used to speak more Spanish.

phrases.target: Todos los días iba al parque.
phrases.en: Every day I would go to the park.
While I was studying, I would listen to music.

phrases.target: Mi abuela tenía un perro grande.
phrases.en: My grandmother had a big dog.

units.grammar_note: The imperfect describes ongoing or habitual past actions ('used to / was -ing'). -ar verbs: -aba/-abas/-aba; -er and -ir share -ía/-ías/-ía. Only ser, ir and ver are irregular.

units.title: Plans with ir a + infinitive
units.goal: Express near-future plans and intentions using ir a + infinitive.

phrases.target: Esta noche voy a comer en casa.
phrases.en: Tonight I'm going to eat at home.

phrases.target: Mañana vamos a visitar el museo.
phrases.en: Tomorrow we're going to visit the museum.

phrases.target: El próximo año voy a viajar a España.
phrases.en: Next year I'm going to travel to Spain.

phrases.target: ¿Qué vas a hacer este fin de semana?
phrases.en: What are you going to do this weekend?
I plan to leave at eight.

units.grammar_note: Conjugate 'ir' in the present, then add 'a' + infinitive. This is the most common way A2 speakers express future — the simple future tense comes later.

units.title: Comparisons & superlatives
units.goal: Compare two things, say which is bigger / better / worse, and form basic superlatives.

phrases.target: El café es más caro que el té.
phrases.en: Coffee is more expensive than tea.

phrases.target: Mi hermana es menor que yo.
phrases.en: My sister is younger than me.

phrases.target: Hablo español tan bien como mi amigo.
phrases.en: I speak Spanish as well as my friend.

phrases.target: Este libro es el mejor de la tienda.
phrases.en: This book is the best in the store.

phrases.target: El tren es más rápido que el autobús.
phrases.en: The train is faster than the bus.

units.grammar_note: Use 'más/menos … que' for unequal comparisons and 'tan … como' for equal ones. 'mejor', 'peor', 'mayor', 'menor' are irregular — never say 'más bueno'.

units.title: Opinions & feelings
units.goal: Give your opinion, agree or disagree, express preferences politely.

phrases.target: Creo que el español es interesante.
phrases.en: I think Spanish is interesting.

phrases.target: Me parece muy importante estudiar todos los días.
phrases.en: It seems very important to me to study every day.
I prefer coffee to tea.
I love Spanish music.

phrases.target: Estoy de acuerdo contigo, tienes razón.
phrases.en: I agree with you, you're right.

units.grammar_note: 'Encantar' works like 'gustar' — the thing is the grammatical subject. 'Me encanta el libro' / 'Me encantan los libros'. Never say 'yo encanto'.

units.title: Past travel & experiences
units.goal: Talk about a past trip — where you went, what you did, what you ate.

phrases.target: El año pasado fui de vacaciones a la playa.
phrases.en: Last year I went on vacation to the beach.

phrases.target: Visitamos tres ciudades en una semana.
phrases.en: We visited three cities in one week.

phrases.target: Conocí a mucha gente en el viaje.
phrases.en: I met a lot of people on the trip.

phrases.target: Compré un regalo para mi madre.
phrases.en: I bought a gift for my mother.

phrases.target: Me quedé en un hotel cerca del centro.
phrases.en: I stayed in a hotel near the center.

units.grammar_note: Use the preterite for completed trip events. 'Conocer' in the preterite means 'to meet for the first time'; in the imperfect it means 'used to know'.

units.title: Health, doctor & pharmacy
units.goal: Describe symptoms, ask for help, follow a doctor's basic instructions.

phrases.target: Me duele la garganta y tengo fiebre.
phrases.en: My throat hurts and I have a fever.

phrases.target: Necesito una cita con el médico.
phrases.en: I need an appointment with the doctor.

phrases.target: El médico me recetó una medicina para la tos.
phrases.en: The doctor prescribed me medicine for the cough.

phrases.target: Tome una pastilla cada ocho horas.
phrases.en: Take one pill every eight hours.
Rest a lot and drink water.

units.grammar_note: Spanish names symptoms with 'tener' or 'doler': 'tengo fiebre' (I have a fever), 'me duele la cabeza' (my head hurts). Body parts take the definite article, not a possessive.

units.title: Work, profession & office
units.goal: Talk about your job, your workplace, your responsibilities and colleagues.

phrases.target: Trabajo en una oficina en el centro.
phrases.en: I work in an office downtown.
My boss is very kind.

phrases.target: Tenemos una reunión a las diez.
phrases.en: We have a meeting at ten.
I'm an English teacher.
I'm very busy this week.

units.grammar_note: Spanish drops the indefinite article with professions after 'ser': 'Soy profesora' (not 'Soy una profesora'). Keep the article only when adding an adjective: 'Soy una profesora paciente'.

units.title: Hobbies & leisure
units.goal: Talk about what you like to do in your free time and how often.

phrases.en: I like to play the guitar.

phrases.target: Los sábados juego al fútbol con mis amigos.
phrases.en: On Saturdays I play soccer with my friends.
My favorite hobby is cooking.

phrases.target: Voy a nadar dos veces por semana.
phrases.en: I go swimming twice a week.

phrases.target: Veo una película todos los viernes.
phrases.en: I watch a movie every Friday.

units.grammar_note: 'Me gusta' + infinitive expresses 'I like to do X': me gusta leer, me gusta bailar. With nouns, agree with the noun: me gusta el fútbol / me gustan los deportes.

units.title: Invitations & polite plans
units.goal: Make and respond to invitations politely; accept, decline, propose alternatives.

vocab.gloss: I'm treating you / I invite you

phrases.en: Would you like to have dinner with me on Saturday?

phrases.target: Me encantaría, gracias por la invitación.
phrases.en: I'd love to, thanks for the invitation.

phrases.target: Lo siento, no puedo, tengo que trabajar.
phrases.en: I'm sorry, I can't, I have to work.

phrases.target: ¿Quedamos a las ocho en la plaza?
phrases.en: Shall we meet at eight in the square?

phrases.target: Quisiera invitarte a mi fiesta de cumpleaños.
phrases.en: I'd like to invite you to my birthday party.

units.grammar_note: 'Quisiera' and 'me encantaría' are the conditional of querer and encantar — softer and more polite than 'quiero' or 'me encanta' for invitations and requests.
